questions.question: Explain the difference between average cost and marginal cost, including the calculation verb for each and the question each one answers.
questions.expected_answer: Average cost divides total cost by output and answers 'what does each unit cost on average so far?' Marginal cost subtracts neighbouring total costs and answers 'what did the last unit alone add to cost?' Average looks at the whole batch; marginal looks only at the latest step.

questions.question: Why does the MR = MC rule find the same answer as computing profit at every output level? Explain the unit-by-unit logic.
questions.expected_answer: Each unit whose marginal revenue exceeds its marginal cost adds to profit, and each unit where marginal cost exceeds marginal revenue subtracts from it. Producing exactly all the profit-adding units and none of the profit-destroying ones must land on the peak of the profit column — so the marginal rule and the brute-force profit calculation agree.

questions.question: The firm earns R40 of profit at six units, which is still positive. In your own words, explain why the firm should nevertheless produce five units, and how you would self-check this answer.
questions.expected_answer: Positive profit is not the test — maximum profit is. The sixth unit costs R38 but earns only R30, so it reduces profit from R48 to R40. Self-check from both sides: the fifth unit still adds profit (MC R26 < MR R30) and the sixth destroys it (MC R38 > MR R30), and the profit column confirms the peak of R48 at five units.
